title: Luc command line
summary: Expose local Distribution, runtime introspection, breaker reset and Cloud source operations through JSON stdout and typed JSON stderr failures.

carrier.notes: Inputs describe normalized CLI arguments; parser evidence gives positional order and literal flag spellings. Defaults include product video and loopback base URL.

replaceability.why: The adapter and layering machinery are the Host foundation. If this machinery could be replaced by a creator layer, automatic fallback to the original could not be guaranteed. The Lucs carried by open protocols have their own replacement classes.
replaceability.decided: Acrab, self-Luc spec v0.3, 2026-10-18; interface charter rule 6, 2026-10-22

reach.notes: Trusted Host machinery, not authority granted to a Luc. Package calls remain bounded by their resolved permissions, Host APIs and editable scope.

operations.name: conform
operations.notes: Holds an Extension to the interface of the Luc it lies on, as the load gate will (lumeri_runtime/luc_interface_gate.py); by default that Luc is the Official Luc this Runtime ships under the id the Extension extends. Nothing is installed or activated. The Luc is taken to hold the permissions it declares, and what the layer would add is listed in asks_for for the creator to approve. Exit 0 when it keeps the interface, 1 when it does not or when no interface contract names the Luc (code and message say why), 2 on a typed failure. Run checks are not part of it yet.

invariants.text: Cloud pull explicitly reports activation_changed false; source delivery does not select a live Runtime.
modules reset removes persisted breaker state and explicitly says it takes effect at next Runtime start.

break: The operation rejects invalid input, integrity, authority or binding state as described by its operation.

conformance.notes: Existing tests listed here were inspected, not run for this documentation task. The area checker validates the contract files; it does not exercise runtime behavior.

known_deviations.text: Typed errors are JSON but Runtime transport failures use SystemExit text and argparse uses its own output. Callers cannot assume all nonzero results are JSON.
list --session returns discovery rather than the local installed graph; modules is the separate live module/fallback view.
